cross_market_insights: The US SERPs are weak: in NY and LA the top organic results for the American-modified queries are Facebook groups, Reddit threads and planner sales pages. The only strong US page is the US Embassy's own requirements list, which has no timeline, no decision help and nothing about life back home. A well-sourced, US-specific planning page has a real chance to rank and to be cited in the AI Overview.

The head term 'get married in italy' in LA returns a 2022 UK-focused Q and A at rank 1 and three paid planner ads, one aimed at couples planning 'from the USA'. Commercial competition is planners, not publishers.

Sydney ranks an exact-match planner domain (marriedinitaly.com.au) first and the Australian Embassy PDF second. AU intent for 'married in italy' is navigational or Australian-legal, so this US article will not win Sydney and should not try. Our general legal guide and the AU-framed pages already serve that market.

Dubai and Singapore show generic 'foreigner' pages (Wise UK guide, Translayte, the US Embassy page). Gulf and Asia readers see whichever nationality guide ranks; nobody serves them by passport. A US page will rank there only for US-modified queries.

Nobody connects the wedding region to the US consular post and the Prefettura in the same consular district (Milan, Florence, Rome, Naples and the consular agencies), so nobody shows couples what their wedding week legal schedule actually looks like.

Nobody explains the six-month validity rule for non-EU documents as a planning constraint (order birth certificates and apostilles in the right window), even though the US Embassy states it. This is the paperwork trap behind the primary persona's first fear.
Nobody covers which Italian consulate in the US handles the Atto Notorio for the couple's state of residence, or what to do if witnesses cannot travel to it.

No ranking page covers what happens back in the US after the wedding beyond 'it is valid': apostille on the Italian certificate, using it for a name change, filing status, insurance. People Also Ask asks 'Are you legally married in the U.S. if you marry abroad?' and 'Do I have to register my marriage in the US?' in both NY and LA.
No ranking page gives the official EUR fees (revenue stamps, Atto Notorio, town hall hire of EUR 500 to EUR 9,200 per the US Embassy) in one place with a USD approximation.

Most planner pages push symbolic ceremonies or packages. None gives an honest decision framework for an American couple: legal in Italy versus a US license plus a symbolic ceremony in Italy, including US license validity windows.
payload.recommended_angle: The US-side playbook for marrying legally in Italy: which documents to order from which US offices and in what order (counted back from the date so nothing expires), what the five or so working days in Italy actually involve by region, what it costs in official fees, and how to make the marriage count back home. Honest about the simpler alternative (marry at home, celebrate in Italy) and about which parts need professional help and which do not.
